CHALLENGE C0005 | Evidence: the apparent `FIND` vs `FINDING_ID` alternation concern is not a bug in the current source. Premises: current terminator is `(...|FOLLOW|FIND|...|FINDING_ID|FINDING)\s*:`. Concrete trace on line `FINDING_ID: F002`: Python tries the `FIND` alternative at the same start position, but it then requires `\s*:` immediately after `FIND`; the next characters are `ING_ID`, so that alternative fails. Regex backtracking then tries the later `FINDING_ID` alternative at the same start position, which succeeds. Therefore `FIND` being earlier in the alternation does not prevent `FINDING_ID:` from terminating the block. VERIFIED: TRUE.

CONFIRM C0025 | Evidence: current `section_terminator` search uses `re.MULTILINE` only. Concrete input with a lowercase next section header:
`ADMISSIBILITY:\nS_min: PASS\nG-completeness: PASS\nd_tool: PASS\nσ_measured: N/A\nq_retest: PASS\nnovelty:\nS_min: FAIL`
does not terminate at `novelty:` because the terminator alternation is case-sensitive. The parser can consume later-section text into the ADMISSIBILITY block, violating the intended section boundary. Adding `re.IGNORECASE` to the terminator search is the simplest sufficient fix. VERIFIED: TRUE.
